title: Areostationary Satellite Station Keeping Via a Natural Motion Trajectory and Predictive Control
summary: Areostationary Mars orbit (AMO) satellites will play an important role in future expeditions to the Martian surface due to their strength as navigation and communication satellites. Perturbative forces experienced by an AMOR satellite will cause it to drift from its nominal orbit, necessitating station keeping. This note presents a novel approach to AMO station keeping that bridges the gap seen in prior predictive control methods between fuel-efficiency and computational-efficiency.
